decision.summary: The Federal Reserve held the federal funds rate steady at 0 to 1/4 percent while launching a new round of mortgage-backed securities purchases.

changes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in August suggests that economic activity has continued to expand at a moderate pace in recent months.
changes.explanation: The Fed noted that economic activity continued at a moderate pace, shifting away from language describing deceleration earlier in the year.

changes.quote: Growth in employment has been slow, and the unemployment rate remains elevated.
changes.explanation: Job growth remains sluggish and the jobless rate is still too high.

changes.quote: The Committee is concerned that, without further policy accommodation, economic growth might not be strong enough to generate sustained improvement in labor market conditions.
changes.explanation: The Fed added a new warning that without extra policy help, growth might stall and fail to improve the labor market.

changes.quote: The housing sector has shown some further signs of improvement, albeit from a depressed level.
changes.explanation: Housing shows slight signs of life though it starts from a very weak place.

changes.quote: Inflation has been subdued, although the prices of some key commodities have increased recently.
changes.explanation: Inflation is mostly quiet, even though a few key commodities saw rising prices.

tone_quotes.quote: The Committee is concerned that, without further policy accommodation, economic growth might not be strong enough to generate sustained improvement in labor market conditions.

To support a stronger economic recovery and to help ensure that inflation, over time, is at the rate most consistent with its dual mandate, the Committee agreed today to increase policy accommodation by purchasing additional agency mortgage-backed securities at a pace of $40 billion per month.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 12.06% APR costs about $50.25 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 1.75% and moved -2 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 3.55% would fall by about $3.36 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 8.1%, and employers added an average of 136k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 1.7% over the past year (August 2012); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.6%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 1.8% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -1 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.09% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that the Fed intends to maintain exceptionally low interest rates at least through mid-2015 and will keep buying assets until the labor market improves substantially. Educational forecast models suggest the next meeting has a 59% chance of a hold and a 40% chance of a cut.

citations.detail: In particular, the Committee also decided today to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent...
